fields.v: Polandra, W. G., Higo, Y., Kula, R. G. (2026). The Role of Agentic Instruction Categories for Code Generation: A Study of Five Python Libraries. Accepted to APSEC 2026 (Asia-Pacific Software Engineering Conference), Technical Track. Read from arXiv:2610.21421v1 [cs.SE], 15 Oct 2026
Conference — APSEC 2026 Technical Track (accepted, per the arXiv comment in slr/exports/arxiv-*-2026-11-18.atom.xml); full text read from arXiv:2610.21421v1, IEEE-style short paper
The University of Osaka, Japan (all three authors)

Compares — 31 combinations of five agent-file instruction categories x 2 LLMs (Gemma 4-26B-A4B, GPT-5.4) in OpenCode, measuring agent-file generation cost (tokens) and compilability, test results and structural similarity of the 5 libraries reconstructed from each agent file

Agent files (AGENTS.md) composed of instruction categories adapted from Chatlatanagulchai et al.: Repository Overview, Function Description, Implementation Detail, Testing, Reconstruction Steps; no version
A single AGENTS.md per condition containing one to five instruction categories (Table I), generated by the agent from the original library

(1) Agent-file generation: OpenCode Plan agent (read-only) plans, Build agent writes AGENTS.md from the human-written library; (2) code generation: in an empty directory with only AGENTS.md, Plan agent produces a development plan (file tree, implementation, testing, verification), Build agent reconstructs the library; (3) compile, run original tests, compute structural metrics
Plan agent before Build agent "allows the human to review and verify the generated plan"; whether humans reviewed plans in the experiment Not stated
Single artefact (agent/context file) used as the only specification for full library reconstruction, run end-to-end with OpenCode
Not classifiable / closest to spec-first (agent file acts as the sole input for regenerating a library from scratch); authors do not use SDD terms
fields.why: The agent file is generated from existing code and then used as the only input to regenerate the library, which resembles spec-first (or even spec-as-source) use, but it is a context file, not a specification, and the authors use no SDD terms
fields.doubt: O AGENTS.md é gerado a partir do código e depois é a única entrada para reconstruir a biblioteca. Decide entre 'not classifiable' e spec-first.

fields.v: New project: reconstruction of an existing library from scratch using only the agent file (authors note it is not a typical SE task); agent file generated from existing code

Automatic: custom OpenCode plugin and .jsonl session logs for tokens; compileall; pytest of original tests; Radon and ctags

Agent: OpenCode (Plan + Build agents). Success criteria stated per library (compiles with python -m compileall; Passed = all original tests pass), but no criterion for when a configuration works; values aggregated per instruction category (16 combinations containing it x 5 libraries = 80 variants per category and model). (1) Agent files + OpenCode + Gemma 4-26B-A4B (local): compile 88.39% overall (RepoOvw 87.50, FuncDec 81.25, ImpDetl 86.25, TestCas 88.75, ReConStp 86.25); Passed 0% for all categories; Partial 13.75-20.00% (FuncDec highest 20.00), overall 17.42%; Failed 80.00-86.25%; agent-file generation tokens 68,070-415,253 (code-generation cost not measured). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors. (2) Agent files + OpenCode + GPT-5.4 (API): compile 98.06% overall (97.50-98.75); Passed 6.25% (ImpDetl) to 16.25% (ReConStp), overall 12.99%; Partial 50.00-58.75% (overall 51.32%); Failed 33.75-36.25%; tokens 78,148-888,781 (highest RepoOvw-FuncDec-ImpDetl-ReConStp on compactor). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors. Structural similarity: total CC and FC close to originals (Gemma within 2.47% for 3 libraries; GPT within 13.58% for 4), LoF and FL far smaller (-16% to -98%)

Tasks: reconstruct 5 trivial Python libraries. Configurations: 31 instruction-category combinations x 2 LLMs (Gemma 4-26B-A4B, GPT-5.4) in one harness (OpenCode); no baseline without agent file. Held constant: prompts (role/directive/context/consideration), harness, agent modes, only AGENTS.md in working directory. Acceptance tests: original human-written test suites, unmodified. Repetitions: 1 run per library and combination. Human intervention: Not stated (plan review possible). Experiments in April 2026

Token usage not determined by number of categories; model and library matter more (compactor highest). GPT-5.4 > Gemma 4 on compile (98.06 vs 88.39%) and tests (12.99% vs 0% full pass). Best category: ReConStp for GPT-5.4 full pass (16.25%, +3.75 points over next), FuncDec for Gemma partial (20%, +1.25). More categories do not improve correctness (best with 1-3 categories). ReConStp most frequent among closest LoF and CC; TestCas and ReConStp for FL and FC. No statistical tests

Distinguished models clearly; differences between instruction categories small (1.25-3.75 points) and not tested for significance. Repeatability: single run per condition. Limitations stated: nondeterminism, agent files leak content across categories, single run, trivial libraries, two LLMs, one harness, one task type

Token usage measures cost not agent-file quality; tests may not cover all behaviour; no maintainability, security, performance evaluation; nondeterminism and prompt sensitivity; categories not isolated in generated files; single run; five trivial Python libraries, two LLMs, one harness (OpenCode), one task; findings preliminary. Future: instruction-level benchmarks, automated instruction selection, larger systems, repetitions, other harnesses and formats

Inconsistencies: filter text requires <= 35 LoF or max CC <= 10, but Table II LoF values are 1,156-26,395 (only CC filter holds); RQ2a answer says Testing had the highest compilation rate, but in Table V GPT-5.4 ties at 98.75% for four categories (Testing highest only for Gemma, 88.75%); Table V has "86,25". Tables III, IV, VII flattened by pdftotext; Table VI values read by column order. Replication package: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.23359831 (agent files, metrics, scripts). Pre-registration: not claimed. Language: Python
